page: Google Cloud Platform c3-standard-4-lssd is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the c3 server family. It is equipped with 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8481C processor operating at 2.7 GHz. The system includes 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance features a bundled 402 GB NVMe SSD, while no GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are provided. The underlying x86_64 architecture supports advanced instruction sets, including Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions and AVX-512.

Benchmark evaluations indicate a clear divergence between single-core and multi-core execution. Single-core metrics, such as the Geekbench single-core score of 1714.0 and stress-ng single-core performance of 1617.89, place the server in the average tier. However, multi-core performance is comparatively weak, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 3812.0 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression speed of 21.7 GB/sec, which falls into the bottom 10 percent of tested systems. Memory bandwidth also registers in the lower quartile, with uncached large-block reads at 29.2 GB/sec and writes at 22.26 GB/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the inclusion of a high-speed 402 GB local NVMe SSD provides strong resource density for disk-heavy operations without requiring external storage attachments. However, the modest 4 vCPU allocation and lower multi-core efficiency suggest that highly parallelized compute tasks may not yield optimal performance per resource. This server is best suited for workloads requiring moderate CPU performance combined with fast local scratch space, such as static web serving, single-threaded text processing, and lightweight database operations.
